chunks: And Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Safwan, from Mu'awiya, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
He commanded the barber to place the comb on his right horn (temple), then commanded him to shave, and he himself named (recited).
"O God, grant me for every hair a light on the Day of Resurrection."
ai.seo_question: What is the supplication recited when shaving the head according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration highlights the Imam’s meticulous attention to ritual grooming, specifically directing the barber to place the comb on the right temple before shaving. The supplication transforms a mundane act into a spiritual investment, where each removed hair becomes a source of divine light (*nur*) on the Day of Resurrection, reflecting the Shia emphasis on finding barakah in daily bodily practices.
